For a lump-sum investment of ₹6 crore growing at 12% annual returns for 20 years, the future value is:

Where:

* P = ₹6 crore
* r = 12\% = 0.12
* n = 20 years

Calculation:

A = 6 \times (1.12)^{20}

(1.12)^{20} \approx 9.646

A \approx 6 \times 9.646 = ₹57.88 \text{ crore}

Corpus after 20 years

≈ ₹57.9 crore

⸻

If you then withdraw ₹1.5 lakh per month

Annual withdrawal:

₹1.5\text{ lakh} \times 12 = ₹18\text{ lakh per year}

But the corpus of ₹57.9 crore earning 12% generates:

57.88 \times 12\% = ₹6.95 \text{ crore per year}

which is about:

₹6.95 \text{ crore} \div 12 \approx ₹57.9 \text{ lakh per month}

You are withdrawing only ₹1.5 lakh/month, while the portfolio is earning about ₹57.9 lakh/month.

Therefore:

* The withdrawal is only about 2.6% of the monthly gains.
* The corpus would not decrease; it would continue to grow rapidly.
* In fact, even after withdrawing ₹18 lakh every year, the corpus would still increase by roughly:

₹6.95 \text{ crore} - ₹0.18 \text{ crore}
= ₹6.77 \text{ crore per year}

So, after 20 years, your corpus is approximately ₹57.9 crore, and withdrawing ₹1.5 lakh per month is easily sustainable indefinitely at a 12% return assumption. The principal would continue compounding and would likely keep increasing over time.
